## Failure signature

On 2026-07-05 the owner reported that the desktop app launched but the window
looked empty. Multiple agents had already verified parts of the app route and
restarted Tauri, but the visible desktop still looked dead.

The decisive split was:

- `tauri-agent-tools health --pid <pid>` reported the webview ready.
- `tauri-agent-tools eval --pid <pid> '...'` showed the SPA route loaded
  (`/adv?tab=harnesses...`), a large `document.body.innerHTML`, no stuck
  `bprogress-busy`, and no error boundary.
- The real X11 toplevel for the same PID reported `WM_STATE: Iconic` and
  `Map State: IsUnMapped` via `xprop` / `xwininfo`.

That means the renderer is not blank. The OS window is hidden/iconified.

## Do not stop at Papercusp

Before patching React, Tauri routes, IPC, or the native terminal, prove whether
the window manager is healthy with a neutral X11 window:

```bash
DISPLAY=:1 setsid xmessage -center 'WM test' >/tmp/xmessage-test.log 2>&1 < /dev/null &
DISPLAY=:1 wmctrl -lxp | rg 'xmessage'
DISPLAY=:1 xprop -id <xmessage-window-id> WM_STATE _NET_WM_DESKTOP _NET_WM_STATE WM_NAME WM_CLASS
DISPLAY=:1 xwininfo -id <xmessage-window-id> -all | rg -n 'Map State|Displayed on desktop' -C 1
```

If even `xmessage` is `WM_STATE: Iconic` / `Map State: IsUnMapped`, this is a
GNOME/Mutter session problem, not a Papercusp app problem. More Tauri
`show()` / `unminimize()` / `set_focus()` calls may be accepted and still fail
visibly because Mutter is auto-iconifying new top-level windows.

## Recovery

On the dev desktop (`DISPLAY=:1`, X11 GNOME Shell), restart Mutter/GNOME Shell:

```bash
DISPLAY=:1 setsid gnome-shell --replace > /tmp/gnome-shell-replace-$(date +%Y%m%d-%H%M%S).log 2>&1 < /dev/null &
```

Wait until the WM is registered again:

```bash
DISPLAY=:1 wmctrl -m
DISPLAY=:1 xprop -root _NET_SUPPORTING_WM_CHECK _NET_CURRENT_DESKTOP _NET_SHOWING_DESKTOP
```

Then activate/move the Papercusp window:

```bash
wid=$(DISPLAY=:1 wmctrl -lxp | awk '$3 == <tauri-pid> { print $1; exit }')
cur=$(DISPLAY=:1 xdotool get_desktop)
DISPLAY=:1 xdotool set_desktop_for_window "$wid" "$cur"
DISPLAY=:1 wmctrl -i -a "$wid"
DISPLAY=:1 xprop -id "$wid" WM_STATE _NET_WM_DESKTOP _NET_WM_STATE
DISPLAY=:1 xwininfo -id "$wid" -all | rg -n 'Map State|Displayed on desktop|Window state' -C 1
```

The expected healthy state is `WM_STATE: Normal`, `Map State: IsViewable`, and
the window on the current desktop.

## Fast diagnostic checklist

Use this order when the owner says the desktop app is blank or missing:

1. Find the live Tauri PID and bridge:

```bash
pgrep -af '/home/dev/.cargo-target/debug/papercusp-desktop|papercusp-desktop'
tauri-agent-tools health --pid <pid>
```

2. Verify the webview, not a browser:

```bash
tauri-agent-tools eval --pid <pid> '(() => ({
  url: location.href,
  title: document.title,
  textLen: document.body?.innerText?.length || 0,
  bodyLen: document.body?.innerHTML?.length || 0,
  bprogress: document.documentElement.classList.contains("bprogress-busy")
}))()'
```

3. Verify the native window:

```bash
wid=$(DISPLAY=:1 wmctrl -lxp | awk '$3 == <pid> { print $1; exit }')
DISPLAY=:1 xprop -id "$wid" _NET_WM_PID WM_STATE _NET_WM_DESKTOP _NET_WM_STATE WM_NAME WM_CLASS
DISPLAY=:1 xwininfo -id "$wid" -all | rg -n 'Map State|Displayed on desktop|Window state' -C 1
```

4. If it is Iconic/unmapped, test a neutral X11 window with `xmessage`. If the
   neutral window is also Iconic/unmapped, restart GNOME Shell/Mutter instead
   of changing Papercusp code.

## Trap that wasted time

Papercusp's glued native terminal can remain visible while the main Tauri window
is hidden. That makes the failure look like a Papercusp split-pane or terminal
glue regression. Disable the terminal (`PAPERCUSP_NATIVE_TERMINAL=0`) to simplify
the picture, but do not treat a still-iconified main window as proof the terminal
caused it.

The app route can also be healthy while the shell window is invisible. Always
cross-check the webview bridge and the native X11 window state before calling a
desktop blank-window incident fixed.
